blocks.raw: # Configure Email
blocks.text: Configure Email

blocks.raw: You can create an email either **from scratch** or by using an **existing email template**.
blocks.text: You can create an email either from scratch or by using an existing email template.

blocks.raw: An **email template** refers to a pre-designed email layout that includes predefined structure, formatting, and placeholders such as <Anchor target="_blank" href="https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/custom-tags">tags</Anchor> and <Anchor target="_blank" href="https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/labels">labels</Anchor>, and sometimes sample content. Templates help maintain brand consistency and reduce the time required to create emails.
blocks.text: An email template refers to a pre-designed email layout that includes predefined structure, formatting, and placeholders such as tags and labels, and sometimes sample content. Templates help maintain brand consistency and reduce the time required to create emails.

blocks.raw: If you choose to use an existing template, you can edit and customize its content, design elements, subject line, and placeholders as needed before saving or publishing the email.
blocks.text: If you choose to use an existing template, you can edit and customize its content, design elements, subject line, and placeholders as needed before saving or publishing the email.

blocks.raw: # Creating a new email from scratch
blocks.text: Creating a new email from scratch

blocks.raw:
1. On the **Engage+** homepage navigate to **Creatives**, section >  **Email tab**, click **Create New**.

2. In the **Creative name**, enter the name for the Email template.

3. **Select the editor for creating the template.** You can choose from the following options:

   * <Anchor target="_blank" href="https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/configure-email#creating-an-email-using-the-html-editor">**HTML Editor**</Anchor> –  Use the basic HTML editor to write and format your email content. If you already have ready HTML, you can copy and paste it directly into the editor.
   * <Anchor target="_blank" href="https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/configure-email#creating-an-email-using-the-drag--drop-editor">**Drag and drop Editor**</Anchor> –Create the email template using the visual drag-and-drop editor. This editor is disabled by default. Raise a ticket with the PST team to enable this option for your organization.
   * <Anchor target="_blank" href="https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/configure-email#creating-an-email-by-uploading-a-zip-file">**Upload ZIP File**</Anchor> –  Upload a ZIP file containing the HTML file and associated images for the template.

   <Image src="https://files.readme.io/a116093402b3c45425e51a98e99dd3900c09e2c2dd10a472c851a20b3e36138f-email-html-editor-google-docs.png" align="center" width="75% " border={true} />

4. Select **Start from Scratch**.

5. Enter the subject and configure the email content based on the editor selected.

6. Click **Create**. To see a preview, select <Anchor target="_blank" href="https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/test-and-preview-across-engagement-channels">**Preview and Test**</Anchor>.

blocks.raw: # Creating an Email using the HTML editor
blocks.text: Creating an Email using the HTML editor

blocks.raw: You can create an email template using the HTML editor either from the **Creatives** section or from the **campaign message creation flow**. The HTML editor allows you to write email content directly in HTML or paste prebuilt HTML and preview it in real time. You can also write or paste <Anchor target="_blank" href="https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/add-dynamic-content-using-liquid">Liquid expressions</Anchor> within the HTML to personalize the email content.
blocks.text: You can create an email template using the HTML editor either from the Creatives section or from the campaign message creation flow. The HTML editor allows you to write email content directly in HTML or paste prebuilt HTML and preview it in real time. You can also write or paste Liquid expressions within the HTML to personalize the email content.

blocks.raw: **Note**: If you want to switch to the CK editor, raise a Jira ticket to the Product Support team to enable it for your organization.
blocks.text: Note: If you want to switch to the CK editor, raise a Jira ticket to the Product Support team to enable it for your organization.

<Callout icon="🚧" theme="warn">

Follow standard email best practices such as [table-based layouts](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/html/html-tables/) and [inline CSS](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/css/inline-css/) to ensure consistent rendering across email clients. Avoid CSS frameworks, external stylesheets, and scripts.
</Callout>

1. From the **Engage+ home page**, navigate to **Creatives** and select **Email**.

   * Use the **preview (right pane)** to view a real-time preview of the rendered content.

Review validation warnings displayed at the bottom of the editor. Below are the types of validation issues you may encounter in the editor: * **Errors:** Displays critical issues in the HTML or Liquid code, such as restricted protocols (for example, `data:` URLs), unclosed or malformed Liquid output tags (missing `}}`), invalid variables, or incomplete control statements (for example, `{% if %}` without `{% endif %}`). Errors must be resolved before you can save the template. * **Warnings**: Displays HTML and content-level validation warnings, including formatting issues such as indentation, spacing, or syntax-related recommendations, unclosed CSS rules, and missing required attributes (for example, missing `alt` attributes for `` elements) **Note**: Each warning includes the line number and character position where the issue occurs. You can still save the template if it contains warnings. However, if the template contains errors, the system will not allow you to save it until all errors are resolved. 8. Use the preview toggle to switch between desktop and mobile views. To expand the preview area, select the **expand icon** in the preview pane. 9. (Optional) Select **Preview and Test** to preview the email and test it with a set of test customers. 10. Select **Done** to save the template.

blocks.raw: ## HTML Editor Validation Messages and Warnings
blocks.text: HTML Editor Validation Messages and Warnings

blocks.raw: While creating or editing an email using the HTML Editor, the system performs multiple checks on the HTML content. These checks help identify invalid markup, unsupported elements, potential security risks, and compatibility issues across email clients and devices.
blocks.text: While creating or editing an email using the HTML Editor, the system performs multiple checks on the HTML content. These checks help identify invalid markup, unsupported elements, potential security risks, and compatibility issues across email clients and devices.

blocks.raw: The following tables describe the validation errors, warnings, and guidance messages that may appear in the editor, along with what each message indicates.
blocks.text: The following tables describe the validation errors, warnings, and guidance messages that may appear in the editor, along with what each message indicates.

blocks.raw: * **Input & Sanitization Errors**
blocks.text: Input & Sanitization Errors

target.note: normalise `*`/`+` markers to `-`

blocks.raw:
| Rule Key                              | Description                                                                                                  |
| :------------------------------------ | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sanitizer.invalidInput`              | The HTML input is invalid. The editor expects the content to be a string.                                    |
| `sanitizer.invalidInputNonEmpty`      | The HTML input must be a non-empty string. Empty content is not allowed.                                     |
| `sanitizer.sanitizationFailed`        | HTML sanitization failed due to an internal error. The error details are displayed for troubleshooting.      |
| `sanitizer.dangerousProtocolDetected` | A potentially dangerous protocol (for example, `javascript:`) was detected and blocked for security reasons. |

blocks.raw:
| **Issue** | **Resolution** | | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **File size is getting reduced** | Expected behavior. File size reduction due to image transformations does not affect user experience. Specify image dimensions to maintain quality. \
For example, if the email specifies a height and width of 200 x 300, images are transformed to match these dimensions instead of saving the original image, which might have very high dimensions. Consequently, the file size is reduced. This reduction could also occur due to dynamic image quality adjustments based on file sizes. | | **Image getting compressed excessively** | Compression varies with file size. Smaller images have less compression; larger images undergo higher compression. This makes sure that irrespective of the file size, similar quality of images is achieved after compression. Do not artificially enlarge images to increase the file size. | | **Images saved in avif format instead of jpeg** | Images are saved in their actual format except when the device supports avif format. avif format enables saving the images in smaller file sizes without impacting image quality. |
